model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for five different model configurations, with the x-axis representing the number of iterations on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 140,000 and the y-axis representing the loss value on a linear scale from 2.4 to 3.4. The five lines correspond to: Vanilla (purple, dashed line), StrmLLM (n=64) (blue, solid line), SepLLM (n=64) (orange, solid line), SepLLM (n=64, H) (green, solid line), and SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (red, solid line), as well as SepLLM (n=128) (dark blue, solid line). All lines begin at a high loss value near 3.4 and exhibit a rapid initial decline, followed by a gradual flattening toward a stable loss value near 2.5 after approximately 100,000 iterations. The Vanilla model starts at a loss of approximately 3.4 and ends near 2.5. The StrmLLM (n=64) line starts near 3.3 and ends near 2.6. The SepLLM (n=64) line starts near 3.3 and ends near 2.5. The SepLLM (n=64, H) line starts near 3.3 and ends near 2.5. The SepLLM (n=64, H/T) line starts near 3.3 and ends near 2.5. The SepLLM (n=128) line starts near 3.3 and ends near 2.5. All lines show a consistent downward trend before leveling off, with the SepLLM variants generally achieving lower final loss values than the Vanilla and StrmLLM models.
